summary: Master Digital Forensics and Incident Response (DFIR). Learn NIST standards, memory forensics, and evidence handling to remediate breaches. Enroll today.
lede: Digital forensics and incident response involves investigating security incidents while preserving digital evidence. For incident responders, forensic investigators and security analysts, the course covers evidence acquisition and chain of custody, Windows and memory artifact analysis, network traffic reconstruction, and malware triage to support incident scoping and clear reporting.
audienceIntro: This course is built for technical professionals responsible for defending organizational assets and investigating security breaches.
audience: Threat Hunters using forensic artifacts to identify
modules: Incident Response Frameworks and Lifecycle Management
Evidence Acquisition and Chain of Custody
Windows Forensic Analysis and Artifact Recovery
Memory Forensics with the Volatility Framework
Cloud Forensics and Remote Incident Response
Advanced Threat Hunting and Adversary Mapping
prerequisites: Participants should have an intermediate understanding of TCP/IP networking, Windows/Linux command-line interfaces, and basic cybersecurity principles. Familiarity with virtualization software (VMware or VirtualBox) is required for lab exercises. Previous experience in a Security Operations Center (SOC) or IT administration role is highly recommended.
